We have mass spec giving m/z 276.0666 as base peak (intensity 100). That likely corresponds to molecular ion [M+H]+? Usually ESI positive mode gives M+H. So M = 275.058? Actually m/z 276.0666 could be M+H, so neutral mass = 275.0589. Let's compute formula candidates. The isomers list gave C15H14ClNO2 (calc mass?). Let's compute monoisotopic mass: C15 = 15*12.0000 = 180. H14 = 14*1.007825 = 14.10955. Cl = 34.968852 (35Cl). N = 14.003074. O2 = 2*15.994915 = 31.98983. Sum = 180 + 14.10955 + 34.968852 + 14.003074 + 31.98983 = 275.071306. Add proton 1.007276 = 276.078582. Slightly higher than observed 276.0666 (difference ~0.012). Could be chlorine 37Cl? 37Cl mass 36.9659, then neutral mass = 276.064? Let's compute with 37Cl: 180 + 14.10955 + 36.9659 + 14.003074 + 31.98983 = 277.068354. Add proton = 278.07563. Not match. Observed 276.0666 suggests maybe formula C14H12ClNO2? Let's compute: C14=168, H12=12.0939, Cl=34.9689, N=14.0031, O2=31.9898 sum = 260. +? Actually 168+12.0939=180.0939, +34.9689=215.0628, +14.0031=229.0659, +31.9898=261.0557. Add proton = 262.0630. Not match.

Maybe formula C15H13ClNO2? mass: C15 180, H13 13.1017, Cl 34.9689, N 14.0031, O2 31.9898 = 273. +? sum = 180+13.1017=193.1017, +34.9689=228.0706, +14.0031=242.0737, +31.9898=274.0635. +H = 275.0708. Not.

Our observed 276.0666 suggests neutral mass 275.0593. Let's try C14H13ClN O2? C14 168, H13 13.1017, Cl 34.9689, N 14.0031, O2 31.9898 = 262. +? sum = 168+13.1017=181.1017, +34.9689=216.0706, +14.0031=230.0737, +31.9898=262.0635. +H = 263.0708. Not.

Maybe formula C16H14ClNO? O1 only? C16 192, H14 14.1095, Cl 34.9689, N 14.0031, O 15.9949 = 271. +? sum = 192+14.1095=206.1095, +34.9689=241.0784, +14.0031=255.0815, +15.9949=271.0764. +H = 272.0837. Not.

Our mass suggests maybe C15H13ClO2? Without N. Compute: C15 180, H13 13.1017, Cl 34.9689, O2 31.9898 = 260. +? sum = 180+13.1017=193.1017, +34.9689=228.0706, +31.9898=260.0604. +H = 261.0677. Not.

Maybe C14H12ClO3? C14 168, H12 12.0939, Cl 34.9689, O3 47.9847 = 262. +? sum = 168+12.0939=180.0939, +34.9689=215.0628, +47.9847=263.0475. +H = 264.0548.

Thus C15H14ClNO2 seems plausible but mass off by 0.012. Could be measurement error? The isotopic pattern shows M+2 peak at 277.0696 intensity 16% which matches chlorine isotopic pattern (35Cl 75% 37Cl 25%). Ratio ~16% of M+2 relative to M is lower than typical 33% for chlorine. But maybe due to instrument. The pattern also shows M+1 at 278.0640 intensity 33% (C13). That seems plausible.

Thus likely formula C15H14ClNO2. So we need SMILES. Among isomers list, we need correct one matching spectra. We haven't looked at NMR. Could get proton NMR to see aromatic patterns. Let's get proton NMR for candidate 1: "CC1=CC(=CC=C1)CNC2=CC(=C(C=C2)C(=O)O)Cl".
